data.disagreement_analysis: The inconclusive verdict from qwen3-235b was caused by an HTTP 400 API error when attempting to audit REUSE.toml, not by any security concern. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed the same file and correctly identified it as benign REUSE licensing metadata. Both models agreed on all other files.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to review REUSE.toml due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), causing inconclusive verdict
learnings: API errors during file review should not cause package-level inconclusive verdicts when the failed file is clearly non-executable metadata (REUSE.toml is licensing configuration)

Models should distinguish between 'file contains no executable code' and 'file could not be analyzed' - the former is a valid safe verdict, the latter should be noted but not block the overall verdict if other evidence is sufficient
Standard VCS packaging patterns (git sources, SKIP checksums, gradle builds) are being correctly identified as safe by both models, indicating good calibration on common AUR patterns
